name: Opening Break — fix 1 (range form)
plain_words: The first 30 minutes set a range. After 10:00, a 5-minute close above the range buys, below it sells; the stop is the other side of the range; one attempt per day, no entries after 12:00, flat by 15:55. The stop is 5–10 times wider than the proven form's, so each tick of cost is a much smaller slice of R — the cost lever, declared as fix 1 of the opening-breakout family.

cost.note: $1.22 per round turn per micro contract + 1 tick slippage per side (2 ticks round trip)

firm.name: futures prop account (Topstep-style 50K)
firm.note: daily loss = self-imposed $1,000; max loss = $2,000 trailing end-of-day; flat before 16:10 ET

pass_line.note: tightened 2026-09-14 before any verdict was adopted: 'sized so the firm's rules hold' is evaluated as the LARGEST risk per trade at which they hold, and the strategy must earn >= 10%/yr of the account at that size — an edge that only survives at a size that earns nothing is not a pass

expectation: Cost per trade falls to about 0.01–0.02R. The signal itself is untested here (the literature's ORB results are modest and unreplicated with slippage). Worst stretch probably still deeper than 10R. Honest odds: 1 in 4. If it fails on the signal (gross ≤ +0.05R), the family's cost lever is closed and only a market fix remains.
